input.body:
Hi Bennett,

Thanks for your email about job NBL-003-2766 (ref R/PM003-1) at Flat 30, 30 Harbour View, Northbridge, ZZ9 0ZZ.

Unfortunately we can't see an attachment on your message. Could you please resend your estimate for the checkout clean, removal of the dumped items and the carpet clean? It would help if you could include the total cost and how it breaks down across those three items.

Many thanks,
Northbridge Lettings

data.reasoning:
Ticket 8 is a duplicate of this same case but contains later events beyond ticket 11's timeline, so I shouldn't use that future information — I can note the duplicate exists without acting on its later content.

My action: reply to the contractor saying no attachment came through on their email and ask them to resend the estimate, then place the ticket on hold pending their response. The inspection report isn't necessary for this decision, so I'll skip reading it.

result.summary: Bennett, the contractor, emailed to say he had attached something and asked us to tell him if it hadn't come through (event 007). There is no attachment on his email in the records, so a reply was needed. I asked him to resend the estimate with the total and how it splits across the clean, the removal of dumped items and the carpet clean. The ticket is on hold until he does, with a follow-up in 2 days. Nothing can be approved until we've seen the estimate.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 006 asks whether the provider needs a reply. They do: event 007 asks us to say if the attachment didn't come through, and no attachment is visible on it. The only file on the ticket is the checkout inspection report the agency sent out. The next step is to get the estimate from the contractor, so asking him is the right move. There is nothing that needs agency judgement.

alternatives_considered.why_not: The contractor asked a direct question and his estimate is missing. Without a reply the job would stall.

alternatives_considered.option: Approve the estimate or pass it to the landlord
alternatives_considered.why_not: No estimate or amount is visible, and the landlord has no recorded approval or spend limit.
The contractor can sort this out himself. There's no conflict, complaint or safety issue.
